analysis:
Examined both workflow excerpts and the complete changed-range map. The executable change sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=prod for qualify-sdk (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml head:239–242); head:181–182 only updates commentary. Build-provider still uses the resolved release environment (head:179–183), and signing still requires successful qualification or the retained-build resume path (head:259–263). The supplied BASE publication and older-macOS validation steps (base:1069–1261) are unchanged.
No concrete security regression is established. Production defaults in the qualification job do not themselves grant production credentials or serving authorization. Qualification has contents:read permissions, while the visible source gate, artifact/source checks and signing prerequisites remain intact. This primarily concerns exact-build qualification and identity assumptions (A-011, A-017, T-054), rather than changes to prompt encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, local helper authority or provider admission.
Integration should examine .github/actions/provider-release-build and Package.swift: the qualification action also receives the resolved environment at head:252–255, so its precedence relative to the new job environment must be verified. Confirm that production-default tests still adequately qualify the separately environment-configured release artifact. Those implementations are not supplied here; their absence is a coverage limit, not evidence of a bypass or unsafe deployment.
